Twenty vials containing 300 mg of enoxaparin each were available in the pharmacy of the space station, but no anticoagulation-reversal agent was available.
Treatment with enoxaparin at a dose of 1.5 mg per kilogram of body weight once daily was started;
the dose was reduced to 1 mg per kilogram once daily after 33 days to extend therapy until oral apixaban could be delivered to the space station with a supply spacecraft.
Transition to apixaban at a dose of 5 mg twice daily occurred 42 days after the diagnosis of venous thrombosis,
and the dose was reduced to 2.5 mg twice daily 3 months after diagnosis.
Protamine and prothrombin complex concentrate were also sent to the space station.
